source.title: A decoder-only foundation model for time-series forecasting
source.authors: Abhimanyu Das; Wei-Hao Kong; Rajat Sen; Yi-Chen Zhou

record.file_problem: None; the full paper and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports a scaling sweep in a different setting and with a different measure: time-series forecasting error rather than language-model held-out cross-entropy.
record.gate_note: The relevant result is the TimesFM scaling sweep in Section 6.2. The paper reports downstream forecasting error against FLOPS, not held-out pretraining loss or a fitted power law. Architecture and data ablations, benchmark comparisons, and fine-tuning results are not rows because they do not test the versions' stated scaling relations.
record.test_reason: A preliminary sweep of 17M/70M/200M time-series models plots zero-shot Monash scaled MAE against FLOPS. This is a new modality, but no power law is fitted and the measure is downstream error, not loss.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors call the scaling study preliminary and say errors 'decrease monotonically with the number of FLOPS (in log scale)'. They make no power-law claim. Their main conclusion is that a 200M decoder-only time-series model reaches near-supervised zero-shot accuracy.
record.recipe_differences: Uses time-series models and downstream scaled MAE, rather than language models and held-out cross-entropy; reports a preliminary compute sweep rather than fitted power laws.

fits_no_version.finding: Zero-shot forecasting error (Monash scaled MAE, geometric mean) falls monotonically with log FLOPS across checkpoints of 17M, 70M and 200M TimesFM models. Values are only plotted (Fig. 3a).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Downstream zero-shot error of time-series foundation models decreases monotonically with training compute.

record.problems: The scaling study is described as preliminary; the text gives no fitted scaling law, numerical checkpoint results, or uncertainty estimates for the Figure 3a trend.
record.rows_left_out: Output patch length and input patch length ablations and the synthetic-data ablation are reported in Section 6.2 and Figure 3, but they test forecasting design choices rather than the versions' specified scaling claims. Fine-tuning and benchmark results likewise do not test a scaling relation.

untested.parts: Whether held-out pretraining loss follows a power law in parameters, data or compute for time-series models. No exponent or fit quality is reported, and data size is not varied.
Language-model pretraining loss is not studied.
No shape sweep at fixed parameter count. Input patch length is varied, but that is a tokenisation choice measured on downstream error.
Language-model downstream tasks are not studied.
No comparison of fits or setups.

missing.what: Numeric checkpoint values behind the scaled MAE vs FLOPS plot. They are needed to judge whether the trend is power-law-like.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V6 'supports' label is dropped: V6 names language models, and the row is a time-series forecaster. For V5, the sweep shows only a monotonic direction on downstream error, with no fit, loss or numbers, so no verdict is given. The FLOPS points are checkpoints from single cosine-schedule runs, which confounds compute with schedule position. The model shape also changes with size (Table 6).

versions.untested_parts: The study does not test held-out language-model pretraining loss as a function of parameters, tokens, or compute.
No power-law fit from small runs or prediction of much larger runs is reported.
The study does not search for or report compute-optimal parameter and token allocations.
The architecture ablations measure forecasting error, not held-out pretraining loss, and do not test the stated claim about loss at fixed parameter count.
Although the models are for time-series forecasting, the study does not test whether the same power-law form holds in another modality or training regime.
The study reports a monotonic trend in downstream forecasting error with FLOPS, but does not fit a predictive relation or test prediction from pretraining loss.
No comparison of fitted exponents, fitting methods, or departures from a single power law is reported.

rows.subject: TimesFM scaling sweep (17M, 70M, 200M)
rows.stage_stated: pretrained; checkpoints from runs trained up to 1.5M iterations
rows.operation_detail: Compared scaled MAE on Monash against FLOPS across checkpoints from models of three parameter sizes.

conditions.value: same pre-training dataset; up to 1.5M iterations; global batch-size 4096

rows.value: The errors decrease monotonically with the number of FLOPS (in log scale).
rows.note: The text states the direction of the trend; the plotted checkpoint values are not given numerically in the text.
rows.check: The reader linked this to V6, but V6 concerns language models; TimesFM is a time-series forecaster, so the row belongs to V5 (other modalities). The text gives only a direction ('errors decrease monotonically'), with no numbers and no fit. The measure is zero-shot downstream scaled MAE, not held-out pretraining loss. The points are intermediate checkpoints of cosine-schedule runs. So the row cannot show whether the power-law form holds. The baseline is correctly not stated.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: TimesFM scaling checkpoints evaluated on Monash
reader_labels.reason: The reported downstream forecasting errors decrease monotonically with FLOPS, supporting improvement with scale in this tested setting; see R1.
